verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: The contract requires /qty in individual pieces. 'Export.Stock pieces' is the only column already labelled in pieces; 'Counts.Cartons' x 'Pack factors.Pieces per carton' is the alternative derivation path, so the quantity source is the one open business fact.

The two quantity paths disagree on the reported figures: for SKU 000001 the workbook shows Stock pieces = 813 while Cartons (3) x Pieces per carton (12) = 36; the same mismatch holds across rows (Counts ranges 3-14, pack factors 6/12/24, so a carton-derived total could never reach 807-1089). That is why /qty is mapped provisionally to Stock pieces at 0.6 confidence.

Export is the only sheet with formula cells (12, one full column, all with cached values, no errors or external links); the formula column should be read from its cached results rather than re-derived, since Counts and Pack factors do not reproduce those numbers.
/sku and /product_name are unambiguous and come only from Export; Counts and Pack factors must not contribute rows (all three sheets share the same 12 SKUs, so no extra population is added).
Pack factors is a lookup, not a second product list; it should not be treated as a products table even though it is keyed by SKU.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Export' is the master list: one row per product (12 distinct SKUs, 12 distinct names, no nulls), matching the operator instruction to use Export as the product list. It carries identity (SKU with leading zeros), the product name, and a per-SKU piece count.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU'; unique per row (12/12), values shown as 000001...000012, i.e. zero-padded identifiers that must be kept as text.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name'; 12 distinct free-text names ('Coffee variant 01', ...) paired one-to-one with SKU, no nulls — the master product description.

columns.name: Stock pieces
columns.reason: Header 'Stock pieces' states the quantity is already in individual pieces, the unit the contract requires; values 807-1089, never null. Confidence lowered because this column holds the sheet's 12 formula cells while the other two sheets provide cartons (Counts) and pieces-per-carton (Pack factors), so the number may be derived rather than typed — and the arithmetic does not reconcile (e.g. SKU 000001: 3 cartons x 12 pieces = 36, not 813).

tables.reason: Sheet 'Counts' holds one stock-on-hand measure per SKU in carton units (3-14 cartons, values increase across SKU 000003...000012), i.e. inventory quantities, not prices, promotions or product attributes. It is a supporting input for piece quantity, not a target field of its own.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Same zero-padded SKU identifier as Export; acts as the join key back to the product master, but the value is taken from Export, so no separate target mapping.

columns.name: Cartons
columns.reason: Header 'Cartons'; whole-number carton counts per SKU (min 3, max 14). Carton is not the contract unit ('individual pieces'), so this is a conversion input rather than a direct /qty mapping; converting requires the Pack factors column.

tables.reason: Sheet 'Pack factors' is a reference/lookup table, not a product, price, stock or promotion list: it maps each SKU to a unit-conversion factor (pieces per carton) with only three distinct factor values (6, 12, 24) repeated across 12 SKUs.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Zero-padded SKU identifier matching Export/Counts; join key for the conversion lookup, no independent target field.

columns.name: Pieces per carton
columns.reason: Header 'Pieces per carton'; low cardinality (6/12/24, 4 SKUs each), the classic pack-size factor used to turn cartons into individual pieces. No target pointer exists — the contract has no pack-size field, only /qty in pieces.
